newsitem.title: JAPAN: Support for Japan PM rises slightly -- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Support for Japan PM rises slightly -- newspaper.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's support rating edged up to 45.4 percent this month, a 1.2 percentage point rise over the previous month, a Japanese newspaper poll showed on Wednesday.
In the first media poll of 1997 to show an increase in support for Hashimoto's 14-month-old administration, the Yomiuri Shimbun said survey respondents gave the government high marks for stability.
However, the weekend survey of 3,000 voters also showed 41.7 percent disapproved of the Hashimoto government, a 0.4 percentage point increase over February.
Most who responded negatively said they did not like the policies of Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), the newspaper said.

The LDP, of which Hashimoto is president, nonetheless garnered the most support among survey respondents, with 33 saying they backed the LDP, against 5.5 percent who expressed support for the main opposition group, the New Frontier Party.
Hashimoto became prime minister in January 1996 at the helm of a coalition of his LDP, the Social Democratic Party and Sakigake, an LDP splinter group.

Following October elections, the 59-year-old Hashimoto formed an all-LDP cabinet, relying on the support of the party's former coalition allies and independents for a working majority in the 500-seat Lower House of Parliament.
